blocks.text: The radio news is the first authentic text that can be followed by ear: it is read in Arabic standard by a conductor who articulates well, has a fixed structure, repeats the main news (titles at the beginning, details after) and uses a few dozen passing formulas. In this unity learn how a news report is made, the formulas that hold it together ( ⁧عَلَى صَعِيدٍ آخَرَ⁩ , ⁧فِي سِيَاقٍ مُتَّصِلٍ⁩ , ⁧أَفَادَ مُرَاسِلُنَا⁩ ), to hear numbers, dates and names said quickly, and a technique of listening in three steps. The news of the unit are simplified and invented; In the last part you start listening to real news (see Appendix C), knowing that at first you will understand the headlines. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 133–134), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, voice synthesis scripts or tutor, a recorder (also the phone), Appendix C for authentic news
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. to recognise the parts of a newsletter and the formulas which introduce them;
2. to understand who is the source of news ( ⁧أَفَادَ⁩ , ⁧نَقَلَ عَنْ⁩ , ⁧ذَكَرَتْ مَصَادِرُ⁩ ) and use correctly ⁧إِنَّ⁩ after ⁧قَالَ⁩ and ⁧أَنَّ⁩ after
other verbs;
3. Listen to a simplified news in three steps and fill out the grid "Chi," what, where, when,
because it does not work;
4. understand numbers, percentages, dates and temperatures at normal speeds;
5. write and read a one-minute news report aloud.

blocks.text: News arrives in order of importance: first domestic and foreign politics, then the economy and society, then sport, finally the weather. Every news begins with the sentence-synthesis (who did what, where, when); The details come later. If you lose the first sentence, you have lost the news: that's why the initial titles are precious.

chapters.title: 7. Numbers, dates and names by ear

blocks.text: Big numbers. On the news they feel whole: ⁧أَلْفَانِ وَخَمْسُمِئَةٍ⁩ 2.500 · ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ مَلَايِينَ⁩ 3.000.000 · ⁧مِلْيَارُ دُولَارٍ⁩ 1 billion dollars · ⁧نِصْفُ مِلْيُونٍ⁩ 500.000. Remember the order: thousands, hundreds, then units before tens ( ⁧خَمْسَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ⁩ = 25). Make it a habit to write the figures as you listen, from left to right, as you hear them: first the thousands, then the hundreds, then leave a place for the tens and write the units. The percentages and decimal places. ⁧خَمْسَةٌ فَاصِلَةُ سَبْعَةٍ بِالمِئَةِ⁩ 5,7% · ⁧رُبْعُ⁩ 1/4 · ⁧ثُلُثُ⁩ 1/3 · ⁧ضِعْفُ⁩ • the double • the double •. The dates. ⁧فِي الخَامِسِ عَشَرَ مِنَ الشَّهْرِ الجَارِي⁩ On 15 This month's ⁧مَطْلَعَ الشَّهْرِ المُقْبِلِ⁩ At the beginning of next month ⁧أَوَاخِرَ العَامِ⁩ At the end of the year. Names. Names of places and entities (ONO-03) often arrive in initial or short form: ⁧الأُمَمُ المُتَّحِدَةُ⁩ , ⁧الاِتِّحَادُ الأُورُوبِّيُّ⁩ , ⁧الجَامِعَةُ العَرَبِيَّةُ⁩ . Foreign names are adapted to Arabic phonetics: ⁧بَارِيس⁩ , ⁧رُومَا⁩ , ⁧مَدْرِيد⁩ , ⁧بُرُوكْسِل⁩ . If you don't recognize a name, write it down how you feel and look for it later.

For the layer 3 use the public broadcasters listed in Appendix C. Choose short news, listen to them in the evening after reading the headlines of the same day on a news site: you will already know what we are talking about. Don't worry if at first you understand the 30–40%: it's normal, and the percentage rises fast if you listen every day.

As a conductor reads. The conductor pronounces all the terminations within the sentence and stops in pause (without desinence) at the end: afāda murāsilunā anna l-wafda waṣala ṣabāḥa I-yawm. It imitates this rhythm: fast inside the group of words, small pause to the comma, longer break to the point. The tanwīn and numbers.
